notes: Use a T-money card for everything. The Climate Card gives 7 days of unlimited travel (~20,000 KRW). AREX to Incheon takes 45 minutes. Naver Map beats Google Maps here.
June to August brings 30°C+ heat and the monsoon (jangma in July). Do palaces in the morning, malls and museums in the afternoon, and the Han River in the evening.
Korean BBQ for two costs 50,000-80,000 KRW; Gwangjang street food costs 5,000-10,000 KRW. No tipping.
Palaces close on Tuesdays (Gyeongbokgung) or Mondays (Changdeokgung). Wearing a hanbok gets you free entry.
Take your passport on the DMZ tour and book 1-2 weeks ahead. The JSA (Panmunjom) is a separate tour and rarely available.
Cafes are part of Seoul culture: try Seongsu, Yeonnam and Ikseon-dong. Coffee costs 5,000-7,000 KRW.

transit.name: T-money / Climate Card
transit.why_chosen: Works on the metro and buses. The 7-day Climate Card is unlimited (~20,000 KRW).

stops.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
stops.tips: The main Joseon palace. The changing of the guard is at 10:00, entry is free if you rent a hanbok (soon 20,000 KRW), closed Tuesdays.

stops.name: National Folk Museum of Korea
stops.tips: A free folk museum inside the palace grounds.

stops.name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
stops.tips: Ginseng chicken soup next to the palace, with queues since 1983.

stops.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
stops.tips: Hanok houses and narrow lanes. Keep quiet, as this is a residential area. There are 8 viewpoints.

stops.name: Insadong
stops.tips: Traditional crafts and tea houses, plus the Ssamziegil courtyard.

backups.name: Gwanghwamun Jip Kimchi Jjigae
backups.tips: Kimchi stew that is cheap and legendary.

backups.name: Changdeokgung Secret Garden
backups.tips: A UNESCO-listed palace with a secret garden. Visits are by timed tour, a swap for Bukchon.

stops.name: Myeongdong Shopping Street
stops.tips: Cosmetics and fashion, with street food stalls out in the afternoon.

stops.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
stops.tips: Kalguksu (hand-cut noodle soup) and mandu dumplings. Michelin Bib Gourmand, since 1966.

stops.name: Namsan Cable Car
stops.tips: Take the cable car up from Myeongdong, or walk up Namsan in 40 minutes.

stops.name: N Seoul Tower
stops.tips: An observation deck and love locks. Stay until 17:00 for sunset.

stops.name: Namdaemun Market
stops.tips: Korea's largest traditional market, with a hotteok (sweet filled pancake) and kalguksu alley.

backups.name: Seoul Museum of Art
backups.tips: A free museum next to Deoksugung, good for a rainy day.

stops.name: Bongeunsa Temple
stops.tips: A Buddhist temple among Gangnam's skyscrapers, with a giant Buddha.

stops.name: Starfield Library COEX
stops.tips: 13 m bookshelves. Free, and great for photos.

stops.name: Gangnam Station Underground
stops.tips: An underground shopping arcade and K-pop stores.

stops.name: Samwon Garden Gangnam
stops.tips: Korean BBQ and galbi since 1976, with a garden setting.

stops.name: Seonjeongneung Royal Tombs
stops.tips: Joseon royal tombs and woodland in the middle of the city. Calm and quiet.

backups.name: Lotte World Tower Seoul Sky
backups.tips: A 555 m observation deck with a glass floor, a swap for the tombs.

stops.name: Gyeongui Line Forest Park
stops.tips: A park on a former railway line, with cafes in Yeonnam-dong.

stops.name: Hongdae Street
stops.tips: A university district with street performances, vintage shops and photo booths.

stops.name: Hongdae Jokbal Street
stops.tips: Pig's trotters (jokbal) and bossam (boiled pork wraps), served to share.

stops.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
stops.tips: A park on the Han River with ramyeon vending machines and bike hire. Picnics in summer.

stops.name: Han River Cruise
stops.tips: A sunset boat from Yeouido, with views of the bridges and skyscrapers.

backups.name: Hongdae Andong Jjimdak
backups.tips: Braised chicken stew in a savoury sauce.

backups.name: 63 Building Art Museum
backups.tips: A golden skyscraper in Yeouido, good for a rainy day.

stops.name: Imjingak Park
stops.tips: DMZ tour (~70,000 KRW). Bring your passport and book 1-2 weeks ahead. No tours on Mondays. See the Freedom Bridge and the bullet-riddled train.

stops.name: Third Infiltration Tunnel
stops.tips: A tunnel dug by North Korea. It is a 350 m sloping walk, and you wear a hard hat.

stops.name: Dora Observatory
stops.tips: Look through binoculars at a North Korean village and a propaganda tower.

stops.name: Dorasan Station
stops.tips: A train station with no trains to Pyongyang.

stops.name: Paju Provence Village
stops.tips: On the way back, a cafe town with a French village theme. Stop for lunch and the bakery.

backups.name: Tongilchon Village Restaurant
backups.tips: Soybean dishes in a DMZ village.

backups.name: Heyri Art Village
backups.tips: An artists' village, a swap for Provence.

stops.name: Jogyesa Temple
stops.tips: The centre of Korean Buddhism, with a lantern festival in May.

stops.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village
stops.tips: Restored hanok cafes and boutiques, on the most photogenic lanes.

stops.name: Gwangjang Market
stops.tips: Bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and mayak gimbap. The market made famous by Netflix, with seating on low stools.

stops.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
stops.tips: A restored stream in the middle of the city, with a 5 km walking path.

stops.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
stops.tips: Zaha Hadid's silver building, with exhibitions and a night market.

backups.name: Ikseon-dong Farm BBQ
backups.tips: Hanwoo (Korean beef) and Iberico BBQ in Ikseon-dong.

stops.name: Seongsu-dong
stops.tips: Seoul's Brooklyn, with old factory cafes and pop-up stores.

stops.name: Seoul Forest
stops.tips: A deer park and ginkgo path, golden in autumn.

stops.name: Onion Seongsu
stops.tips: A cafe in a former factory, with pastries and coffee for a farewell treat.

stops.name: Seoul Station AREX
stops.tips: The AREX express to Incheon takes 45 minutes. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Seongsu Galbi
backups.tips: Galbi, a swap for the cafe.

backups.name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
backups.tips: A riverside park, a swap for the forest.
